title: Planaria regenerate barium-insensitive heads after barium-induced head loss

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Planaria regenerate barium-insensitive heads after barium-induced head loss

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Planaria exposed to barium, a non-specific potassium channel blocker, lose their heads but soon regenerate heads that are completely insensitive to barium, by transcriptionally regulating relatively few genes; the authors interpret this as cells navigating transcriptional space to solve a novel physiological stressor not met in evolution.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: A Proposal for a Framework › Specific Conceptual Components of the Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere Framework

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: For example, when planaria are exposed to barium, a non-specific potassium channel blocker, their heads explode. Remarkably, they soon regenerate heads that are completely insensitive to barium (Emmons-Bell et al., 2019).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds”, Frontiers in systems neuroscience (2022), doi:10.3389/fnsys.2022.768201; section “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: A Proposal for a Framework › Specific Conceptual Components of the Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere Framework”. Scope: Planarian flatworms chronically exposed to barium chloride

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-tame-11: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.66

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Head loss, regeneration, resistance, and transcript counts are explicit endpoints with published experimental support. Existing data can check the biological result, while the problem-solving interpretation remains only a proxy.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare head integrity, regeneration, subsequent barium survival, and gene-expression change in chronically exposed and control planaria, testing whether regenerated heads acquire resistance with a limited transcriptional response.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Raw survival and morphology records may not be deposited.

The interpretation as navigating transcriptional space is not uniquely implied by resistance.

data adequacy: 0.42
data existence: 0.55
discriminating power: 0.74
analysis feasibility: 0.7

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The expression half is in a public RNA-seq series and can be reanalyzed with a standard differential-expression pipeline. Phenotype claims, that heads are lost and the regenerated heads are barium-insensitive, sit in the paper's counts with no separate deposited assay table. The navigational reading of those gene changes is not separated by the expression matrix from a narrower physiological compensation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reanalyze GSE98084 for the fraction of transcripts that change in barium-adapted heads versus wild-type heads, and compare that count with the paper's survival and regeneration tallies in BaCl2; the transcriptional clause holds if only a small fraction of the transcriptome moves.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Differential expression does not show that the cells searched transcriptional space for a solution evolution had not already produced.

Two biological replicates limit how firmly 'relatively few genes' can be reestimated.

Head loss and later barium insensitivity are phenotype counts in the paper, not in the expression series.
